Results.ReviewText: Previously, the wife and I always used propane for grilling because of the ease of using a propane grill. However, we decided to make a switch and she surprised me with the Pro Series 34. Right out of the box, the instructions are clear (it’s easy to assemble). The two wired thermometers it provides are great and accurate. It’s very sturdy and holds heat very well. The hopper for the pellets is large and will hold MORE than enough for what you’re cooking. It looks sorta like an offset smoker, but better because you just set the temp on the dial and it does all the work for you by feeding the right amount of pellets (which there’s a bunch to choose from) to keep the cook going instead of having to tend to it yourself. Our first cook on it was ribeyes. The aroma coming off these steaks was INCREDIBLE! I would’ve eaten boot leather if it came off the Traeger smelling like that! It was also the juiciest steak I’ve ever had outside of Ruth Chris’s. If you’re worried about price, it’s WELL WORTH IT! You’ll never need another grill. Not to mention you’ll never switch back to propane or charcoal after you taste the difference. We’re going to be making our turkey on it for thanksgiving and we can’t wait! Neither can our guests.
Results.Title: Worth every penny!

ClientResponses.Response: Hey Phil. Welcome to the Traegerhood. We're stoked to have you here with us. Thank you for taking the time to leave us a review on your new Pro 34. Having to replace a component on our new grills is not a common occurrence, but if replacing the temperature probe on your Traeger did not fix the issue, we're more than happy to continue helping to make it right. Are you using the insulation blanket that you mentioned when the grill is overshooting the set temperatures? If so, at what temperature is the outside air at the time of use? Using the insulation blankets in warmer weather can cause damage to the blanket, grill, and can become a fire hazard. We also have the option of looking for a local dealer in your area with a service tech to help replace any parts that may need maintenance, if you're uncomfortable with working on the grill yourself. Results.ReviewText:
I’ve owned my Pro 34 for less than three months and have used it three times.  The first cook went well.  During the second cook the temperature swings were crazy.  I had it set at 180, and the swings went from 90 to 315.  I called Traeger and they figured the problem was likely the RTD sensor (temperature sensor).  They promptly sent me a replacement.  The instructions to replace it were pretty simple and I had no issues changing the part.

Yesterday I fired up the grill for a third time.  Temperature set at 180.  For the first Three hours the temperature fluctuated between 175 and 220.  While this is a big swing, I can live with it.  After hour 3, the temperature went to 280-295 and was not dropping.  I decided to just turn off the grill.

This is a three month old pellet grill.  Why is it my responsibility to change parts on the grill?  I believe Traeger should figure out a way to do that for me.  And, I still have the temperature problem.  Not quite sure what to do at this point.  I am very good about not opening the lid, and I purchased the Traeger insulation blanket.

Thus far, I am very disappointed in this product.

ClientResponses.Response:
Hey NJ Camper, thanks for taking the time to review your Pro 22.

When going for a sear on your Traeger, take your temp as high on the dial as your model goes. For best results, we're shooting for 450-500 degrees Fahrenheit. Allow time for the cooking surface to come up to temp before loading on your meat.  Once you’re preheated, you’re ready to go.

Gently lay the meat on the grates. Searing time varies depending on the type and cut of meat but generally, you’ll want to sear for just 3-5 uninterrupted minutes per side.

Don’t touch it until it’s time to flip. If you poke and prod at it, you could release juices prematurely which will ruin your sear. Use tongs, a spatula, or our pig tail BBQ flipper to flip.

These tips and many more can be found in the Explore section of our website. Don't hesitate to reach out to us at 1-800-TRAEGER if you have any questions or concerns, we're happy to help.

ClientResponses.Response:
Hey James, thanks for taking the time to review your Pro 34.

That temperature readout does need addressing based on the pictures you've shown. This isn't a common issue, but we can absolutely help get you up and Traegering again. We would recommend the troubleshooting starts with your RTD, or Resistance Temperature Detector, inside your grill's barrel.

The best way to test your RTD is by comparing the ambient temperature of the grill to the external temperature. With the grill cooled down, turn on your grill and take note of what temperature shows up on the controller. Compare this to the outside temperature, either using a third-party thermometer or the current daily temperature. Acceptable temperature variation is within 20°F/10°C. The temperature variation may be larger when the grill is sitting in the sun.

If the readings are more than 20°F/10°C off, please contact our support team at 1-800-TRAEGER for assistance. These troubleshooting steps and more are also available in the Support section of our website.

Hey Wingerit, thanks for taking the time to review your Pro 22.

A key to understanding Traeger grills is that they cook at an average temperature, meaning that there may be some slight fluctuation higher or lower than the set temperature. Your home electric oven does the same thing, producing an average temperature over the course of the cook.

On a typical, good-weather day, your grill should fluctuate no more than ±15°F. If your grill is fluctuating more than that, some troubleshooting may be required. Results.ReviewText: I purchased this for myself as a birthday gift about a year ago. Great quality and pretty much does as described. As with others, I have occasionally had temperature fluctuations and one incident of pellets burnt in the auger at the fire box. After doing my research and following instructions provided by Traeger, I discovered that the pellets that were left in the hopper and auger had adsorbed just a touch of the ambient humidity during a rare damp period (I live in the SW desert). I replaced the pellets and everything works very well. I use the grill cover religiously and leave as few pellets as possible in the hopper/auger as a pop-up storm during the monsoon season could be an issue. I love the flavor blends in the Traeger pellets and have smoked/grilled just about every kind of meat, poultry, and fish as well as select veggies. The cleanup can be a bit of a pain with needing to shop vac out the residue after each use but overall love this product.

ClientResponses.Response:
Hey L,

It's unfortunate that you experienced that, here’s how we would like to help you. Let's start with the pellet quality, Pellets may be compromised if they are light in colour, not shiny, dusty, break easily, or the bag has lots of sawdust in it, they could easily get stuck at the end of the augur. If you ran out of pellets and the auger is completely empty, you would most likely notice a drop in temp and possibly the grill shut itself off completely. If this is the case, wait for the grill to cool and put your food in the oven to keep it warm. Once the grill has cooled, pull out the grate, drip tray, and heat baffle. Look in the fire pot to ensure it is not full of pellets. If it is, clean out the fire pot. After the fire pot is empty, put the grill on high and wait for the auger to become filled with pellets. Once you start to see pellets fall into the fire pot again, turn the grill off and place the internal pieces back into the grill. At this point you will be able to restart your cook. It is always a good habit to check the pellet level in the hopper whenever you go out to check your meat. We recommend checking the support page on our website for tips regarding  Pro series 34 grill maintenance and temp swings. Our technical team can be reached at 1800 - TRAEGER if you have further questions or require assistance.

ClientResponses.Response:
Hi there, we would suggest using Hickory or Mesquite pellets and cooking at low temps for longer periods of time for a more smokey flavor. 
Our grills produce a varying amount of smoke based on the cooking temp. Low temperatures (165°F - 225°F) produce the most smoke, anything higher than 225°F will produce next to zero smoke.

Results.ReviewText:
9/6/2020 @ 5:30pm 
I started the Traeger via the smoke mode. As normal, after the smoke engaged I turned the temp to 450 degrees and closed the lid (preparing to cook steaks). 
A few minutes later I went to check the temp and noticed it displayed a temp in the 500's which I have never seen before. 
I quickly opened the lid and flames were fully engulfing the unit and rapidly increasing. 
Flames were at approximately 7' high just under the patio cover so my wife called 911. 
I then grabbed a towel to hold the side handle and pulled the Traeger out from under the patio and began dousing it with water from the garden hose. 
Fire dept arrived and checked the patio cover structure for any problems and determined we were "very lucky the house did not catch fire.". 

9/7/2020  
Called Traeger (1-800-TRAEGER) and spoke to David. Recapped yesterday’s incident and he said to email a description and include supporting pictures. 

I sent the email and pictures to supportverification@traegergrills.com.

 9/8/2020 @8:45am
Called Traeger and spoke to Charlise. I asked if she had received my email and she said yes, looking at it now. She then said she would review with her supervisor and put me on hold for 18 minutes. Charlene then came back to the phone and said “since you are past the 3 year warranty there was nothing she could do for me.” I then asked to speak directly to the supervisor. She put me on hold for another 10 minutes. 
After 10 minutes Charlise came back and put her supervisor (Nathaniel) on the line and she dropped.  I asked Nathaniel if he has reviewed the pictures and supporting documentation and he confirmed he had. He said “those pictures are scary”. I said yes, my house cam very close to catching fire. 
Nathaniel then went on to say there is no coverage due to being past the 3 year warranty. I reiterated the fact that if my house had caught fire we would be having a different conversation. I am just looking for Traeger to back their product and help me get into a replacement Traeger. Nathaniel then said “sorry nothing I can do”. I then said this is a horrible display of customer service and I am very disappointed. Call ended.
Results.Title: Traeger catches fire, almost burns the house

Results.ReviewText: I’ve grilled and smoked for many years, but never on a pellet smoker.  I live in Logan Utah about five miles from Camp Chef headquarters.  After doing much research I decided the best bang for the buck was the Traeger brand.  I’m not disappointed either.  First, the build quality of my Traeger appears much better.  Second, Traeger is much more established in the pellet grill market having decades more experience.  Third, this is much more versatile than any other grill I’ve ever owned.  It has more cooking space.  The heat is more evenly distributed.  I’m able to smoke, grill, and bake with it with zero flame ups and easy starting.  I was even able to season my cast iron with it at 450 degrees.  The flavor is amazing as well.  It’s as if I cooked it over a fire of the wood the pellets list.  Third, the app has many different recipes.  Their Facebook page has new cooks showing you ideas for uses all the time.  Finally, their instructions are in English only.  I don’t have to flip through a massive book of multiple languages to find the English section.  I look forward to many years of use and when this wears out.  I’ll likely buy another one.  Would rate a five star plus if possible

Results.ReviewText: After many years standing outside “grill sitting,” I finally dove in and spent the money on a new Traeger Pro 34.  I had talked myself out of it many times and went through 2 grills in the meantime.  I had an offset smoker for the past 6 years and I finally tired of loading wood chunks and charcoal in it.  Standing outside in 100 degree heat trying to maintain an even temp etc, got to be old shoe.  I had been eyeing this Traeger for a long time and I finally bought it.  What a difference, no matter what you want to cook, you just do your prep, preheat the grill, lay your food inside and go back in the house where it’s air conditioned.  Go back after set time and your food is cooked to perfection, not looking like it escaped the crematorium.  Meat is tender and juicy every single time.  Veggies are amazing as well. Heck, I even smoked pineapple rings and they were excellent. I wish I could set this grill in my house, I would toss my stove out to the curb.  If you’ve been thinking of springing fora Traeger don’t wait, just do it, I promise you won’t regret it.
